01 Problem · in plain words

Rubbish keeps coming back. Reports go nowhere.

Residents have no simple way to report public rubbish, and today’s channels treat every report as a separate complaint. So the same spots stay dirty.

1

Rubbish appears

beside a walkway, park or drain

2

Few report it

3 in 4 never do

3

Reports pile up

as separate complaints, none ranked

4

It stays, and comes back

no priority, no follow-up

01 Our users · 44 residents surveyed, 14–18 Nov 2026

They care. They just don’t know where to go.

The resident · main user

“Where do I even report this?”

Walks past the same rubbish every day. Doesn’t know which council to call, and never hears back.

Needs: one easy way to report, and proof something happened.

Township manager · decision user

“Which case is urgent?”

Gets many complaints about the same pile through different channels.

Needs: one case per spot, ranked by urgency.

39.4%of non-reporters don’t know where to report
59.1%motivated by recognition
56.8%want progress updates
52.3%worry about fake reports

“Send reports directly to the correct local council”

“Allow follow-up photos if rubbish remains”

02 Solution · watch it happen

One photo. Five steps.

1

Report

Snap a photo. The app saves the location.

2

Verify

AI checks waste type, severity and public land.

3

Merge

Same rubbish, one hotspot. One confirmation per account.

4

Prioritise

3 residents or 3 days, and it turns URGENT.

5

Track

Followed to Resolved. Residents earn EcoPoints.

Block C walkway0 / 3 confirmationsNO REPORTAI scan is simulated in the prototype

Not the report. What happens after it.

Ten reports, one pileTen separate complaints→One hotspot
Which comes firstNo way to rank urgency→Ranked automatically
After reportingResidents rarely hear back→Tracked to Resolved
